name: musepack
why: An old audio codec with its own tools; a sideways look at how lossy audio formats were built before MP3 won.

brief.what_it_is: Musepack (MPC) is a lossy audio compression format and its associated tools. The homepage describes it as an audio compression format with a strong emphasis on high quality, not lossless, but designed for transparency so the author says listeners can't hear differences from the original WAV file. The brew entry lists these executables: mpc2sv8, mpcchap, mpccut, mpcdec, mpcenc, mpcgain, wavcmp. The homepage does not describe what each one does, so their roles are not confirmed from the page. The format takes WAV audio in and produces much smaller MPC files, and decoders turn MPC back into audio.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a high-quality format for listeners who value sound quality plus storage and processing efficiency, and it stresses that it is open source under the BSD license and patent-free. It says the format has been stable since Stream Version 8 in 2007.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says Musepack is based on MPEG-1 Layer-2 (MP2) algorithms, extended since 1997 with heavily optimized, patentless code. It also says the encoder's psychoacoustic model was tuned to be transparent at the --standard setting, with little tuning for low bitrates. The page does not explain the bitstream or the encoder internals in more detail.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists downloads for Windows, Linux and Mac OS X, plus a source code/library page and an SVN repository. No install steps, runtime requirements or configuration appear on the homepage. The brew entry adds no caveats.
brief.standout: The homepage makes a speed claim: on devices running Rockbox firmware, Musepack decodes faster than Vorbis, AAC and MP3, which the author ties to longer battery life on low-power hardware. It is also an old codec built on MP2 that its own page says was tuned for high bitrates rather than low ones, which runs against most modern codecs.
brief.status: quiet. The page shows a 'Project Status' item dated 2024.09.29 saying the format is stable and there is 'no intention to fix what is not broken', but the latest news item is dated 2012.12.29 and the footer reads '© 2003-2016'. No release or commit dates were visible on the homepage.
brief.caveats: The author concedes it is not particularly optimized for low bitrates; AAC, Vorbis and WMA are presented as better there. The homepage's claims of transparency and top listening-test results come from the author and cited community tests, not independent verification here. Platform support is listed as Windows, Linux and Mac OS X. The homepage was fetched but no README, commands or install docs were available to read.
quotes: Musepack is an audio compression format with a strong emphasis on high quality. It's not lossless, but it is designed for transparency
The Musepack audio format has been stable and robust since the release of Stream Version 8 in 2007.
There is no intention to fix what is not broken.
fetch_log: https://www.musepack.net/ - fetched OK; homepage text used as the source. Not a GitHub repo, so no README. Did not follow further links: the homepage has no command examples, and I did not guess other URLs.
